text:
ingrid: Heads up — saw a spike in schema rejects for the formatter tool on /invoke-tool. ~3.2k in the last 10m, mostly array vs object mismatch.

drew: Got an alert, can you paste a sample payload?
ingrid: sure. snippet from the logs:

```
REQUEST: route=/invoke-tool formatter v2
RESPONSE BODY:
{"tool":"formatter","output":["line1","line2"]}
VALIDATION ERROR: expected object with key \"formatted\", got array
```

priya: That looks like the strict validator on v2 rejecting older adapter outputs. Is this from the canary we turned on this morning?

ingrid: yes, 10% canary started at 07:12. Router routed some older adapters to v2 because of a routing hash change. Fallback policy currently returns 400 and marks the call as failed.

sam: Oof. Two problems: 1) UX — callers see hard failures 2) telemetry/billing — failures are counted as errors, customers might be charged differently.

ops-bot: alert: canary-toggle changed by @drew at 07:12:08 — strict-validate=true for variant v2

drew: I did the toggle to tighten schemas. Didn't expect older adapter outputs to still be live. We should avoid hard-reject for first rollout.

priya: Proposal: add a soft-validate mode for rollouts. Soft mode logs a schema_reject metric with tags but lets the response through (and tags the response in tracing). That way console shows rejects without breaking customer traffic.

sam: Agree. Implementation notes: runtime should add header `X-Validate-Mode: soft|strict` and set route.status = "soft_reject" when soft mode sees mismatch. Billing pipeline needs to treat soft_reject as success for charge semantics.

drew: Also need better metric labels. Right now our `toolcall.schema_rejects_total` has no variant label. Add `route`, `variant`, `model_id`, `customer_tier`. Makes it easier to filter in dashboards.

ingrid: Quick viz suggestion for console: show a sample of rejected payloads (redacted) under Rollouts -> Variant -> Schema rejects. Add a one-click rewind (route to fallback variant) from that UI.

priya: We should be careful with samples for PII. Sampling + redact by existing redaction pipeline before storing. Add sampling rate default 0.1% for console samples.

sam: From runtime side, fallback behavior: currently fallback policy is `no-fallback` -> return 400. We should add an option `fallback: route-to-previous-variant` or `fallback: allow-soft-pass`. For canaries, default to soft-pass.

drew: I'll open a runtime PR to add `X-Validate-Mode` and fallback modes. Also will wire metric labels.

ingrid: I'll do a quick patch to the router so we don't route adapter shards with old signatures to strict variants during canary. Might reduce blast radius.

priya: Console work — I'll sketch the UI. Need a backend endpoint to fetch samples + metric series. Endpoint should accept `since` and `sample_rate` and return redacted strings.

sam: Billing: @finance-infra FYI — we need to ensure `soft_reject` flows into `chargeable_success` in the billing join. Otherwise customers may get unexpected invoice diffs.

deploy-bot: canary rollback suggestion: Based on schema_reject spike > 1% of traffic in 10m, recommended action: revert strict-validate toggle.

drew: I'll temporarily rollback the canary to 0% until soft-mode is in place.

ingrid: Action items summarized:
- drew: PR to runtime for `X-Validate-Mode` and new fallback modes (+ metric labels)
- ingrid: router patch to avoid routing legacy adapters into strict variants during canary
- priya: console sample UI + backfill endpoint (with redaction + sampling)
- sam: coordinate billing mapping for soft_reject -> success semantics
- ops team: backfill telemetry for the last 24h to verify how long this was happening

priya: Anyone object to soft-validate default for future canaries?

drew: No objections. Makes rollouts safer.
ingrid: Good. Reverting canary now, starting hotfix branch for soft-validate.

sam: Thanks all. I'll add a short blurb in Rollouts doc about schema-safe canaries.

ingrid: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: action: canary set to 0% at 07:24:40 by @drew

drew: PR links incoming in #prs shortly.

ingrid: closing loop — once soft-mode merged, let's run a 1% canary with sampling enabled and watch `sum(rate(toolcall.schema_rejects_total[5m])) by (route,variant)` and `toolcall.soft_reject_rate` on console.

sam: ETA for changes? Drew: 2-3h for runtime patch; Priya: wireframe by EOD; Billing: Sam will loop in finance infra today.

ingrid: thanks — this avoided a broader outage.
